title: Cosmological Implications of the Slingshot Effect: Gravitational Waves, Primordial Black Holes and Dark Matter
summary: In this paper, we explore the implications of the so-called slingshot effect. It represents a rather general phenomenon occurring when a localized source, such as a monopole, quark, or a $D$-brane, crosses a domain wall separating the confined (Higgsed) and unconfined (Coulomb) phases of the crossing source. The crossover is accompanied by a stretched ``string'' of proper co-dimensionality that confines the source to the domain wall.
